transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I came in because things at work have gotten to where I can’t just shrug them off anymore. I operate industrial trucks at the warehouse, been around that kind of work a long time, and lately the routing system there—the computer that tells you where to go, what to pick up, what scanner to use—it doesn’t feel like just a computer anymore.

I know how that sounds, but it’s like it’s been marking my movements. Not just tracking like normal work tracking, but marking me specifically. The scanners, the little beeps and the messages that come through, they’re not random to me. They’re sending things in a way that feels directed, like nudging me, pushing me out. Like the system knows I’m one of the old hands there and it wants me gone, or somebody’s using it that way. I’ve been trying to keep my head down and do the job, but it’s gotten heavy enough that I figured I needed to talk to somebody before it gets worse.
Do you believe the computer system is actually capable of knowing your thoughts or intentions?

I don’t know if I’d put it like it can read every thought in my head, like some science fiction thing, but… it knows more than it should. That’s what bothers me. It’s not just sending me to aisle 12 or telling me which pallet to move. It’s the way it lines things up, the timing, the scanner beeps, the messages that pop up right when I’m thinking, “Okay, just do the next job and stay out of trouble.”

It feels directed at me. Like it’s marking my movements and, I don’t know, picking up on what I’m going to do before I do it. Or somebody behind it is. The system knows I’m one of the old hands there, and it’s been pushing me, steering me, making it clear I’m not wanted. So whether it knows my thoughts exactly… I can’t prove that in words. But it knows my intentions enough to send those messages and move me around like it’s trying to get me out.
Do you feel like you're being marked or targeted outside of work as well?

Mostly at work. That’s where it’s clearest, where I can actually see the pattern happening in front of me — the routing system, the scanner messages, the way the jobs get assigned, the timing of the beeps. That’s where I know I’m being marked, because it’s not just a general system doing general things. It’s been marking my moves and sending things through those scanners in a way that feels aimed right at me, like it’s trying to push me out because I’ve been there a long time, one of the old hands.

Outside of work… I don’t know. I don’t want to make it bigger than what I can point to. It’s more like I carry the feeling with me after I leave, because once you’ve spent a whole shift feeling like the system is tracking you personally and trying to steer you, it doesn’t just shut off when you get in the car. But the main targeting, the actual messages, that’s at the warehouse. That’s where it’s happening.
Do you ever have times when you don't believe the computer system is targeting you?

There might be little moments where I try to tell myself, “Maybe it’s just the system doing what it does,” you know, because I’m not trying to make trouble out of nothing. I’ve worked around equipment and computers long enough to know they assign routes and track productivity and all that. I understand that part.

But when I’m actually there, standing with the scanner in my hand, and the routing system starts lining things up the way it does—the beeps, the messages, sending me certain places at certain times—it’s hard to not see what’s happening. It’s not just a computer to me anymore. It has been marking my moves. That’s the part I keep coming back to.

So, do I ever not believe it? Maybe for a few minutes if I’m away from it, or if I’m trying to calm myself down. But once I’m back on the floor, it feels clear again. It’s sending messages through those scanners, pushing me, like it wants me out because I’m one of the old hands there. I don’t really get much relief from that thought once the shift gets going.
Do you think it's possible that your interpretation of the computer system's behavior could be wrong?

I mean… I understand why you’re asking that. Part of me knows people can misread things, especially when you’re tired and you’ve been on the floor all day with the scanner going off and the routes changing. I’m not saying I have a printout somewhere that says, “This is aimed at you,” you know?

But it doesn’t feel like just an interpretation to me. That’s the problem. I’m here because the routing system at the warehouse isn’t just a computer to me anymore. It’s been marking my moves. The scanner messages, the way they come through, the timing of them, where it sends me—it feels like it’s pushing me out because I’m one of the old hands there.

So could I be wrong in some abstract way? I suppose anybody could be wrong about anything. But when I’m there and it’s happening, it doesn’t feel wrong. It feels clear. It feels like the system knows where I am, what I’m doing, and it’s sending those messages to steer me, to make it harder on me, to get me gone. That’s what I keep seeing.
Do you think it's possible for you to change your mind about the computer system targeting you?

I don’t know how to answer that cleanly. I can say the words, like, “Sure, maybe I could change my mind if there was some clear explanation,” but sitting here saying that is different from being back on the warehouse floor with that scanner in my hand.

Because when I’m there, it doesn’t feel like a belief I just chose. It feels like something I’ve watched happen over and over. The routing system isn’t just acting like a regular computer anymore, not to me. It marks my moves — where I am, what I’m doing, when I’m doing it — and then those messages come through the scanner in a way that feels aimed right at me. It’s like it’s steering me, pushing me, making the work harder, like it wants me out because I’ve been there so long, one of the old hands.

So could I change my mind? Maybe if it stopped, or if someone could show me exactly why all those messages and routes line up the way they do. But right now, no, not really. Not while it keeps happening the same way. I know what it feels like when a machine is just assigning work, and this feels different. It feels personal.
Would finding out that the routing system's behavior is due to a software glitch or a new efficiency protocol change your belief about it targeting you?

If somebody told me it was a software glitch or some new efficiency protocol, I’d listen, I really would. I’m not trying to be stubborn just for the sake of it. I’ve worked long enough around equipment and systems to know companies change procedures, computers mess up, management rolls out new things and doesn’t explain them right. So on paper, yes, I can understand how that could be an explanation.

But the thing is… that doesn’t really cover what it feels like when it’s happening to me. It’s not just one odd route or one strange scanner message. It’s the way the routing system at the warehouse has been marking my moves, like it knows where I am and what I’m doing, and then the messages come through the scanners at just the right times. It feels aimed at me. It feels like it’s pushing me, wearing me down, trying to move me out because I’m one of the old hands there.

So if they said “glitch,” I’d want to know why the glitch keeps lining up around me. If they said “efficiency protocol,” I’d want to know why that protocol seems to land on me the way it does. Maybe it would make me quiet down for a little while, maybe I’d try to accept it, but I don’t think it would really change what I believe unless it explained all of it. Because right now, to me, it’s not just a computer doing computer things. It’s personal.
Have you ever had a period of time, even if just a day or two, where you didn't feel like the computer system was targeting you?

A whole day or two? No… not really, not once it started feeling this way.

I mean, there might be moments when I’m away from the warehouse, or when I’m busy with something else, where I’m not actively thinking about it every second. Like if I’m driving home or trying to get through dinner, I can sometimes push it to the side for a little bit. But that’s different from not believing it. It’s still there in the back of my mind, because I know what’s been happening.

When I’m back on the floor, with the scanner in my hand, it comes right back clear as day. The routing system isn’t just assigning work like a normal computer anymore. It’s been marking my moves — where I am, what I’m doing — and then the scanner messages come through in a way that feels aimed at me. Not random. Not just business as usual. It feels like it’s steering me and wearing me down, trying to push me out because I’m one of the old hands there.

So no, I don’t think I’ve had a stretch where I truly felt, “Oh, it’s not targeting me.” Maybe I’ve had short breaks where I wasn’t staring straight at it, but I haven’t stopped knowing it’s happening.
Have you ever woken up in the morning feeling like the computer system is not targeting you?

No… I can’t say I’ve woken up and felt like, “Oh, it’s not happening.” Not once it got into my head the way it has.

Some mornings I wake up and for a few seconds I’m just thinking about getting my coffee, getting dressed, my back hurting, whatever normal thing is there first. But then it comes back in. I remember I have to go back into that warehouse, and that routing system is waiting there, and the scanner is going to start up again with those messages. It’s not like I wake up with a clean slate and think it’s just a regular computer.

I know how it sounds when I say it out loud, but to me it isn’t just a machine assigning routes anymore. It’s been marking where I go, what I’m doing, how I’m moving around the floor, and then the scanner messages come through in a way that feels directed at me. Like it’s trying to steer me into mistakes or wear me down until I leave, because I’ve been there a long time. I’m one of the old hands there.

So mornings might be quieter for a minute, before I’m actually at work, but the belief doesn’t go away. I still know it’s targeting me.
Do you think there's a specific person behind the computer system that's targeting you?

I don’t know if I can put a name to a person, like say, “It’s him” or “It’s her.” I’m not saying I’ve seen somebody sitting at a keyboard with my name on the screen or anything like that. But I have a hard time believing it’s just the computer doing it all by itself.

The routing system at the warehouse… it’s not just a computer to me anymore. It’s been marking my moves — where I am, what I’m doing, how I’m moving around — and then the scanner messages come through in a way that feels like they’re meant for me. Like it’s pushing me, steering me, setting me up to look bad or wear me down. And I keep coming back to the same thing: I’ve been there a long time. I’m one of the old hands there. Maybe somebody wants me gone and they’re using the system to do it.

So no, I don’t have one specific person I can point to. But it feels like there’s intent behind it. It feels too directed to be random.
Do you think the computer system or whoever might be behind it is only targeting you while you're at work?

Mostly it happens through work, yes… I mean, that’s where the routing system is. That’s where the scanners are. That’s where it can mark where I am and what I’m doing and send those messages through, the ones that feel like they’re meant to push me around or make me mess up.

But I wouldn’t say it’s only at work in the sense that I just clock out and it disappears. When I’m home, the scanner isn’t in my hand, so it’s not happening in the same direct way. But I still know what it’s doing. I still think about how it’s waiting there, how it’s been building this picture of my movements and steering things against me. It kind of comes home with me in my head, if that makes sense.

The actual targeting, the way I experience it most clearly, is on the warehouse floor. That’s where it has access to me. That’s where it sends the messages and routes me a certain way, and it feels like it’s trying to wear me down because I’ve been there so long. Like I’m one of the old hands and it wants me out.

So… not exactly only at work, but work is where it’s active. Home is more where I’m thinking about what it’s already doing and what it’s going to do when I go back.
Can you think of any specific incident or event at work that first made you feel like the computer system was targeting you?

I can think of the shift where it really clicked for me, yes. I don’t know if I can give you the exact day, but it was at the warehouse, with the routing system and the handheld scanner. I’d been there long enough to know what normal glitches look like, what a bad assignment looks like, what random confusion looks like. This didn’t feel like that.

It started with the way the routes were coming through. It kept sending me in these patterns that didn’t make sense, like back and forth, out of order, making me look slow or like I wasn’t keeping up. And then the scanner messages — the little prompts and corrections — they started feeling too pointed. Not just “go here” or “scan this,” but like the timing of them was aimed at me, like it was watching how I moved and then pushing me into the next mistake.

That was the first time I remember thinking, this isn’t just a computer assigning work. It’s marking where I go. It knows my moves. And it’s using those scanner messages to push me, to wear me down, like it wants me out because I’m one of the old hands there.

I know someone else might say it was just the system being inefficient, but I’ve worked around that kind of equipment a long time. This felt different. It felt directed at me.
Have you ever had a period of more than a week where you didn't feel like the computer system was targeting you?

No… not really. I mean, maybe there were days where I didn’t talk about it as much, or I tried to keep my head down and just do the job, but more than a week where I didn’t feel it was happening? No, I can’t say that.

Once I understood what the routing system was doing, it didn’t just go away. That’s part of why I’m here, because it isn’t just a computer to me anymore. It’s been marking my moves at the warehouse — where I go, how fast I’m moving, what aisles I’m sent to — and then the scanner messages come through in ways that feel like they’re pushing me, correcting me, setting me up. Like it’s trying to make me look bad or make me worn down enough to leave.

Some shifts are worse than others, sure. There might be a day where it’s quieter, or I think, okay, maybe I can get through today without it coming down on me so hard. But even then I still know it’s there, still tracking and building off what I do. I’m one of the old hands there, and that’s what keeps sticking in my mind — that it’s pushing me out because I’ve been there so long.

So, no, I don’t think I’ve had a full week where I truly felt free of it. It’s been there in one way or another.
Have you ever had a moment where you completely stopped believing the computer system was targeting you?

No… I don’t think I ever completely stopped believing it. I’ve had moments where I’ve tried to talk myself down, like, “Maybe it’s just the routing system being messed up,” or “Maybe everybody’s scanner is acting strange today.” I can say that, and I’ve tried to say that to myself because I don’t want to be walking around upset all the time.

But underneath that, no, I still know what it’s doing. That’s why I’m here, really. The routing system at the warehouse isn’t just a computer to me anymore. It’s been marking my moves — where I go, how it sends me from one place to another, how the scanner messages come in at just the right time to push me or make me look like I’m falling behind. It feels directed. It feels like it’s trying to push me out because I’m one of the old hands there.

So maybe there are minutes, or part of a shift, where I try not to focus on it as much. But completely stopped believing it? No. I don’t think that’s happened.
Have you ever had a moment, no matter how brief, where you didn't think the computer system was targeting you?

Maybe for a few seconds at a time, if I’m being honest… like if I’m distracted by lifting something, or talking to somebody, or just trying to get through a task. But even then, it’s not like I really stop believing it. It’s more like I push it to the side because I have to keep working.

I’m here because the routing system at the warehouse isn’t just a computer to me anymore. I know it’s been marking my moves — where it sends me, how it changes the route, how the scanner messages come through — and it feels like those messages are meant to push me out. Like they’re trying to wear me down because I’m one of the old hands there.

So if you mean, did I ever have a clear moment where I thought, “No, this isn’t happening, it’s just a normal system,” then no. Not really. I might try to tell myself that for a moment, but I don’t believe it deep down. It always comes back to the same thing: it knows what I’m doing, and it’s using the scanners and routing to push me.
Did anything significant change at work or in your personal life around the time you started feeling like the computer system was targeting you?

Yeah… yes, there was a change. It didn’t come out of nowhere. It started after they changed the warehouse routing system, when they put in that newer way of sending us around, and around that same time they moved us onto rotating overnight shifts.

That’s when I started noticing it. I mean, not all in one single minute like a light switch, but that’s when it began to feel different. Before that I knew the place, I knew the routines, I knew how the work flowed. Then the system changed, the scanner started directing things differently, and with the overnights rotating around, everything felt off — like I couldn’t get my footing the same way.

It’s been going on about two years and three months now, if I’m counting right. I remember because it was tied to that change at work. The routing system came in, the shifts changed, and after that it just… it started feeling like the system wasn’t just assigning work anymore, like it had turned toward me somehow.
Do you ever feel like people or things outside of the warehouse, like on the street or at home, are watching you or trying to send you messages?

Not really in the same way, no. I mean… I can get on edge outside of work because I’m already carrying it around in my head, you know? If I’ve had a bad shift, I might still be thinking about what the scanner did or why it sent me a certain way, and then I’m tense when I’m driving home or sitting at home. But the actual thing, the targeting, that’s the warehouse system.

That’s why I keep coming back to the routing computer and the scanners. It’s not just a machine assigning tasks anymore. It knows where I’m going, it marks my moves, it sends those scanner messages at just the right times, and it’s trying to push me out because I’ve been there a long time — I’m one of the old hands. That’s where the messages are coming through.

So on the street or at home… I don’t know, I wouldn’t say people out there are sending me messages. It’s more that the warehouse system stays with me after I leave because I know I have to go back to it.
Do you think anything or anyone else, besides the warehouse computer system, is trying to target or harm you?

I don’t think it’s anyone else in the same way. I mean, I’m not saying every person is out to get me or something like that. It’s really centered on that system at work — the routing computer, the scanners, the way it sends me places and times things.

That’s what I keep trying to explain. It isn’t just a computer to me anymore. It’s been marking my movements, watching where I go in the warehouse, and those scanner messages… they don’t feel random. They come through in a way that feels directed at me, like it’s trying to wear me down or make me look bad so I’ll leave. Because I’ve been there a long time, I’m one of the old hands, and it feels like the system has turned on people like me.

So if you mean, do I think some other person outside of that is trying to harm me, no, not really. But the warehouse system itself — yes. That’s the thing targeting me.
Do you think you are being targeted or watched by anything or anyone outside of the warehouse computer system?

No, not outside of that, not really. I don’t feel like people on the street or neighbors or anything like that are watching me. It’s the warehouse system. That’s why I keep saying it’s not just a regular computer to me anymore.

The routing system knows where I’m going, it marks my moves, and then the scanner messages come through at these times that feel… aimed at me. Like it’s trying to make me look slow, or send me in circles, or put me in situations where I’ll mess up. And I think it’s because I’ve been there a long time — I’m one of the old hands — and it wants to push me out.

So if you mean outside the warehouse computer system, no, I don’t think there’s some other person or thing doing it. It’s that system. That’s what’s targeting me.
Do you feel like you're being targeted or watched by anything or anyone when you're not at work?

When I’m not at work, I don’t really think it’s a separate person or something following me around, if that’s what you mean. It’s not like I’m walking down the street thinking every car or neighbor is part of it.

But… it does stay with me. Because I know I have to go back there. The routing system at the warehouse, that’s the thing. It’s not just a computer to me anymore. I know it’s been marking my moves, watching where I go in the building, and then sending messages through the scanners in these ways that feel like they’re meant for me. Like it’s trying to push me out because I’ve been there so long — I’m one of the old hands.

So at home, no, I wouldn’t say something new is watching me there. But I’m still thinking about what the system did, what it sent me, why it sent me there, and what it’s going to do next shift. It kind of follows me in my head, but the targeting itself is from the warehouse system.
